record.context_brief: high-dimensional classification of positive sectional curvature
record.original_question: Conjecture: in every dimension n ≥ 25, every compact manifold with positive sectional curvature is diffeomorphic to a rank-one symmetric space.

evidence.quote: Question 4.3 (Conjecture). For dimension n≥ 25, all compact manifolds with positive sectional curvature are diffeomorphic to rank-one symmetric spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A compact rank-one symmetric space is a compact Riemannian symmetric space of rank one; up to isometry (and rescaling), the simply connected examples are the spheres S^n, the complex projective spaces CP^n, the quaternionic projective spaces HP^n, and the Cayley projective plane CaP^2 (together with their quotients by isometric free actions, e.g. real projective spaces). All known examples of positively curved compact Riemannian manifolds in dimension ≥ 25 are diffeomorphic to such rank-one symmetric spaces.

Prove or disprove the following: for every integer n ≥ 25, every closed (compact, without boundary) smooth n-dimensional Riemannian manifold admitting a metric of positive sectional curvature is diffeomorphic to a rank-one symmetric space.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of compact manifolds with positive sectional curvature in high dimensions remains a central open problem in Riemannian geometry. All known examples in dimensions ≥ 25 are rank-one symmetric spaces (the only sporadic non-symmetric examples occur in dimensions 6, 7, 12, 13, and 24), but no proof of the conjectured classification is known. Surveys by Ziller and others list this as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Manifolds with Positive Sectional Curvature (Ziller)
status_evidence.snippet: Apart from compact rank one symmetric spaces, only sporadic examples of manifolds with sec > 0 are known in dimensions 6, 7, 12, 13 and 24.
status_evidence.claim: No new examples of positively curved manifolds are known in dimensions ≥ 25 beyond rank-one symmetric spaces, and the classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Non-Negative Sectional Curvature (compiled by M. Kerin, AIM)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems list including conjectures on the classification of positively curved manifolds in high dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is recorded as an open problem in differential geometry.
